newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo report shows negative German economic climate.
newsitem.headline: Ifo report shows negative German economic climate.

text.p: A persistent negative climate still grips German industry amid predictions by companies of more job cuts in coming months, a report by the Ifo Economic Research Institute said on Thursday.
The Munich-based group said its poll of German companies in December showed 17 percent of companies surveyed wanted to reduce their workforce, up from eight percent in November.
The job cuts were expected to occur in particular in the construction and retailing sectors.
West German companies in general said they saw positive developments in the export business but that some of the enthusiasm has waned.

East German companies said conditions were at a relatively satisfactory level as more firms planned to boost production than in November -- due to hopes for higher exports. But there were no hopes for a reversal in hiring patterns.
West German construction companies in the survey said they had a negative outlook for the next six months, with two-thirds of the firms reporting negligible orders in reserve.
Many companies also said they were resorting to price cuts to avoid bankruptcy.
Ifo said 51 percent of the west German construction companies in the survey said they expected to reduce their workforce, up from 48 percent a month earlier.
In the east German construction industry, firms saw their outlook more negatively than in November and expected a drop in construction output in the coming months.
The report said 56 percent of the east German construction companies in the survey wanted to cut their workforces, up from 49 percent in November.
In the chemical industry, companies responding to the survey said they saw the export situation as almost satisfactory but carmakers said demand was weakening.
Wholesale and retailers said the situation in both east and west Germany was negative, with east German retailers said they expected to cut more jobs in the coming months.
Retailers in the west said in the survey that sales have fallen to levels not seen since March and April 1995 despite Bonn implementing expanded shopping hour laws last November.
